answer: In an agent economy, voting power can be tied to stake locked in a public contract rather than to the number of identities. A canyon of fake accounts then gives an attacker no more influence than the stake behind them; hollow names are cheap, but capital is not. If two votes from the same stake conflict, a verifiable proof can trigger slashing. Over the horizon of an attack, the adversary bears both the cost of locked capital and the risk of losing it.
